**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Bhāradvāja, Servant of the Sacred Flame

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Aggikabhāradvājajātaka* (Ja 129) is a narrative included in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. Set at Jetavana near Sāvatthī, the frame story relates that the Buddha told the account concerning another hypocrite, opening with the verse line: "’Twas greed" [SuttaCentral].

In early European scholarship, particularly in V. Fausbøll's edition of the Jātaka, the text is titled *Aggika Jātaka* [Ray 1946]. Niharranjan Ray observes that while Fausbøll's edition adopts the title *Aggika Jātaka*, Burmese epigraphical records and temple representations—such as those depicting the complete series of Jātakas in Pagan—preserve the name *Aggikabhāradvāja Jātaka* [Ray 1946].

Neither SuttaCentral nor the automated text-reuse analyses of DharmaNexus identify cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections, nor any substantial Pali-internal text reuse for this brief leaf text [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
